message.reasoning_content:
Analyze the fast inverse sqrt accuracy. Key risk: 2 Newton iterations may not reach 1e-6 absolute over whole FP16 range (|x| up to 65504). For large x, inverse_length ≈ 1/|x|, value ≈ ±1. Error depends on rsqrt accuracy ~ relative 4e-4 after seed... Fast inverse sqrt error after 2 iterations ~ relative ~1.7e-6? Actually seed rel error ~3.4% -> 1 iter: ~0.17% -> 2: ~5e-6 relative. Output value up to ~1, so absolute error up to ~5e-6 > 1e-6. Also target near 1 for large x, and value = x*inv where x ~ 65504. Potential failure. Also intermediate FP32 rounding of 1+x*x at large x: x*x=4.3e9, adding 1 loses precision — but target defined on exact stored FP16 value, so rounding 1+x² to FP32 introduces error. 1+x² with x=65504: x²=4294070016, +1 in FP32 rounds to 4294967296? FP32 ulp at 4.3e9 is 512, so 1 is lost — relative error ~1e-10, fine. Bigger: FP32 x exact (x² rounding ~1e-7 relative) — sqrt halves it; then inverse sqrt Newton error dominates. So risk: 2 Newton iterations insufficient for 1e-6 absolute tolerance. Also bitcast trick: squared_length is computed with fused ops? enable_fp_fusion=False, so not fused — bitcast of FP32 value fine. Also N as tl.constexpr causes recompile per size — fine. Masking correct. Output FP32 correct.
